events.summary: Country: Afghanistan Source: Save the Children KABUL, 18 November 2026 – More than half of children displaced in Afghanistan said they have less food to eat since leaving their homes, while two in five reported worsening health, according to a new Save the Children report that reveals the severe toll displacement is taking on children across the country. The “Children on the Move” report, based on interviews with more than 800 children and caregivers in seven provinces in Afghanistan, found that displacement over the past three years has deepened hunger, disrupted education and exposed children to heightened protection risks. More than nine in 10 children surveyed had experienced displacement or migration. More than half (55%) of children said they had less food to eat after moving, 41% said their health had deteriorated, and a third (33%) of caregivers said children's access to education had worsened. But despite growing needs, support is failing to reach many children. Fewer than one in 10 children surveyed said they had received any assistance, while nine in 10 said they needed support to access food. events.title: Notice of Revised National Environmental Policy Act Implementing Procedures
events.summary: Homeland Security Department. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS or Department) is updating DHS Directive 023, Implementation of the National Environmental Policy Act, which establishes procedures for complying with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). This update is necessary in light of the recent rescission of the Council on Environmental Quality's NEPA implementing regulations, which DHS's procedures were designed to supplement. In addition, the update incorporates provisions from the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act; and the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 related to the environmental review process. The updated Directive promotes collaboration and efficiencies in the implementation of NEPA and modernizes the processes and procedures for environmental review. This update enables DHS to conduct coordinated, consistent, predictable, and timely environmental reviews, thus reducing unnecessary burdens and delays. The draft Directive is being made available for public review and comment. These comments will inform development of the final Directive. Upon finalization, the Directive will rescind DHS Directive 023-01, Rev 01 and DHS Instruction 023-01-001-01, Rev 01 which were issued in 2014.

The exercise assessed key areas of South Sudan’s Ebola preparedness efforts, including case management, infection prevention and control, laboratory capacity, contact tracing and coordination.
